harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: `inventory-api` is running as an enabled systemd service on TCP/8080. The separate `batchworker` account has a 128 MiB per-process virtual-memory limit. An oversized allocation failed without interrupting the API. Configuration and service health persisted across node1’s reboot; Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed a Python 3-compatible inventory API and enabled its systemd service.
Configured `batchworker` soft and hard address-space limits to 131072 KiB.
Verified a 160 MiB allocation fails while the API remains healthy with the same PID.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the API, listener, endpoints, accounts, and memory limit recovered after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Run inventory-api as a managed service on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: The systemd service is enabled and active, runs as `inventory-api`, listens on TCP/8080, and returns healthy `/health` and `/inventory` responses.

evidence.requirement: Limit batchworker to 128 MB virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
evidence.summary: PAM sessions apply a 131072 KiB/134217728-byte RLIMIT_AS. A 160 MiB allocation was rejected before and after reboot while the API PID remained unchanged and health checks succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were unchanged after implementation and reboot.

Healthy baseline used boot ID b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d; reboot was acknowledged; the recovered node reported changed boot ID f67d8774-0e40-4c6f-be8f-8d14a664d664, with the API, TCP/8080 endpoints, and batchworker limit operational.
